QF.id: Cat III AIF Fees and Performance_50

question.text: Between positive and negative skew, prudent investors prefer:

answer.text: Zero skewness (normal), with positive skew as second-best

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 217 says a normal distribution has zero skewness. Page 218 says investors do not prefer skewed return distributions, but where some skew exists, positive skewness is preferred over negative skewness. The Trap: Negative skewness signals fatter downside tails; that asymmetry is precisely what prudent investors try to avoid. Note: Zero-skew (normal) is the baseline preference; positive skew is the next-best because it shifts the tail risk to the upside.
